Hi Sarah / Marissa - quick technical proposal below based on the ask for 0-retention of user content and reduced log windows. Trying to strike a balance between Nimbus' privacy needs and operational debugability.

Proposal (production-ready options):
1) 0-retention customer profile (recommended for PHI-sensitive flows)
   - User content: not persisted to long-term storage. Transit-only processing; ephemeral copies exist only in-memory and are wiped as soon as inference completes.
   - Short-lived debug buffer: optional ephemeral buffer retained for up to 72 hours; accessible only with customer auth and audit trail.
   - Audit logs: only metadata (timestamp, request id, model variant) retained for 90 days for compliance; payloads excluded.

2) Masked ingestion pipeline (recommended if you need some retention for analytics)
   - PII redaction at ingest (server-side) for configurable fields (SSN/MRN/email) + tokenization option.
   - Retained logs (masked) for 30 days by default, configurable down to 7 days.

3) Hybrid: 0-retention for content, 7-30 day retention for operational logs (request_id, latency, error codes) to satisfy SRE/observability. No request/response payload retention unless explicitly enabled via signed exception.

Security artifacts to attach: SOC 2 summary (attached), DPA template with suggested redlines (I'll add comments where we need negotiated language).

Constraints / trade-offs:
- 0-retention disables some post-hoc debugging; we can enable a time-limited debug snapshot mechanism that requires customer consent and is fully auditable.
- Some platform features (long-term evals, quality monitoring) rely on retained queries; if you need those, we recommend tokenized retention.

I've attached a proposed retention schedule spreadsheet with the concrete TTLs and a DPA with redlines. Happy to jump on a call with your legal/security to walk through the language.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
